name: Help Scout
tagline: Shared inbox, knowledge base, and live chat for small support teams.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: A single-person shared inbox is genuinely buildable: pull mail over IMAP, thread it by message-id, tag it, write replies back out over SMTP. The hard part is not the UI, it is everything around deliverability and multi-agent coordination: domain authentication, bounce handling, collision detection when two people open the same conversation, and the audit trail that makes support work auditable. Help Scout also bundles a public knowledge base, chat widget, and a pile of integrations that each take their own afternoon. If you are a solo founder answering support from one address, the DIY version is honestly fine and arguably nicer. If you have a team and customers who expect replies that land in the inbox rather than spam, the gap is real.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app that syncs a support mailbox over IMAP, threads messages into conversations, lets you tag, assign, snooze, and reply with saved snippets, and sends replies back out over SMTP.
requirements: An email account with IMAP and SMTP access, app password in .env
A domain with SPF, DKIM, and DMARC configured if you want replies to land
Node and a local Postgres or SQLite file
Patience for IMAP edge cases: threading, quoting, and HTML mail are all gross
whatYouLose: Deliverability as a service: Help Scout manages sending reputation so your replies do not land in spam
Collision detection and real presence, so two teammates do not answer the same ticket twice
The hosted knowledge base and chat widget, which are separate products bolted on for free
Dozens of ready integrations: Shopify, Jira, Slack, HubSpot, plus the API and webhooks
Reporting that a manager will accept: response time, resolution rate, happiness ratings
moatNotes: The email part is commodity. The part where five people work one inbox without stepping on each other, and the part where the reply actually arrives, are not.
whyPeopleStillPay: Support is one of those jobs where the tool failing is immediately a customer-facing failure. If your homegrown inbox drops a message, double-sends, or starts getting flagged as spam, you find out from an angry user, not a dashboard. Teams pay per seat because the alternative is one person becoming the permanent on-call maintainer of the inbox software, which costs more than the seats. Solo operators are a different story and often do fine with a plain shared mailbox plus some tooling.
notes: Great for one person, dicey for five. The multi-agent coordination is where the money is.
prompt:
Build a local, single-user support inbox web app. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non-negotiable:
- Next.js (App Router) with TypeScript
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/inbox.db
- Tailwind for styling, no component library
- imapflow for reading mail, nodemailer for sending, mailparser for parsing

Secrets in .env.local only, never committed: IMAP_HOST, IMAP_PORT, IMAP_USER, IMAP_PASS, SMTP_HOST, SMTP_PORT, SMTP_USER, SMTP_PASS, SUPPORT_FROM. Ship a .env.example.

In scope:
- A sync script (npm run sync) that connects over IMAP, fetches new messages from INBOX, parses them, and stores them.
- Threading: group messages into conversations using In-Reply-To and References headers, falling back to normalized subject plus sender.
- Conversation list view: status (open, snoozed, closed), tags, last message preview, sorted by most recent activity.
- Conversation detail view: full message history, collapse quoted text, render HTML mail inside a sandboxed iframe, show plain text when available.
- Reply composer that sends over SMTP, sets In-Reply-To and References correctly, and stores the sent message in the conversation.
- Saved replies (snippets) stored in SQLite, insertable into the composer with variable substitution for {{customer_name}}.
- Tags, open/close, and snooze-until-date. A snoozed conversation reopens when its date passes.
- Full-text search over message bodies using SQLite FTS5.
- Keyboard shortcuts: j/k to move, e to close, r to reply, / to search.

Out of scope, do not build:
- Multi-user, assignment, permissions, or presence
- Public knowledge base or chat widget
- Third-party integrations or webhooks
- Analytics dashboards, satisfaction ratings, SLA tracking

Seed the database with three fake conversations so the UI is usable before IMAP is configured. Write a README that explains how to get an app password, what SPF/DKIM/DMARC are and why replies may land in spam without them, and how to run the sync on a cron.
